target_customer: Maintenance and facilities teams at small and mid-size businesses and later enterprises, paying per user per month
problem: Maintenance work orders and asset history were tracked on paper or in clunky desktop CMMS software, so technicians in the field lost time and companies lost visibility into asset costs.
business_model: B2B SaaS per seat subscription (starter plans about 25 USD per user per month in 2017)
product_category: Mobile-first CMMS and enterprise asset management

founders.name: Ryan Chan
founders.background_notes: Worked as a process development engineer, then taught himself iOS development and built the first app. Sources differ on whether work began in 2015 or 2016.

competitors.name: Fiix
competitors.what: Cloud CMMS with a mobile work order tool
competitors.traction_then: Established vendor; no figures in the source

competitors.name: SAP and IBM
competitors.what: Enterprise asset management with desktop tools described as clunky

technical_complexity.rationale: A mobile and web work order app is standard engineering. The solo founder built the first version himself as an iOS engineer, and hard parts were mostly offline mobile sync and scanning.

defensibility.rationale: Many CMMS vendors existed and the feature set was easy to copy. Stickiness came from stored asset and work order history once adopted.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents added mobile apps over time and MaintainX launched in 2018 as a mobile-first rival, but UpKeep kept growing and raised a Series B in 2020.

market_need_then: Per the 2018 press release, about 80 percent of organizations still used manual maintenance management tools. TechCrunch in January 2017 reported 240 paying customers just after moving from a free app to paid plans.

branding.domain_note: Early material used onupkeep.com; the company later moved to upkeep.com. Dates and purchase terms not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain, approachable voice; YC launch post pitched it as Basecamp for facility maintenance teams

branding.community_and_virality: A maintenance community content hub existed under the Maintenance Hero name on the early domain; no evidence of merch or fan activity.

brand_strength.rationale: A clear descriptive name that fits the product and has stayed constant for ten years, but no sourced evidence of the brand itself driving growth.

outcome_analysis: UpKeep went from a founder built mobile app to 240 paying customers at Demo Day in early 2017, then raised a 2.7M seed in June 2017, a 10M Series A in March 2018 and a 36M Series B in May 2020, reaching a reported 4,000 plus customers. It won by attacking desktop era incumbents with a cheap per user mobile product. In May 2026 it announced a strategic growth investment from Accel-KKR.
notes: Directory status says Acquired, but the only transaction found is a May 2026 strategic growth investment from Accel-KKR (amount undisclosed, not described as an acquisition), so exit type is unknown. YC page claims 50M total raised; press totals reach 48.8M after the Series B. Founding year 2015 or 2016 depending on source.
